name: Saoirse Agyemang-Dzelzkalns
location: Pilsen Veil, runs a studio called Dermis & Ghost out of a converted freight container, near Halsted and Division
description:
Saoirse is compact and deliberate in movement, with dark olive skin covered from throat to ankle in her own accumulated work — a living portfolio in bioluminescent pigment, dermal sculpture, and chromatic scale-pattern geneware that shifts between copper and deep teal depending on her body temperature. Her canines are cosmetically elongated and slightly iridescent, a piece she did on herself at twenty-two that she now considers slightly embarrassing but has kept because removal would leave scars. Her hair is a complex architectural shape, natural black at the root and heat-reactive at the tips, changing from rust to amber when she's working close to the pigment-heating instruments.

Saoirse's reputation in Pilsen Veil is built on what regulars call 'the consultation' — a two-hour process before any work begins, in which she asks questions about the client's life that seem invasive until the finished piece makes them make sense. She treats body modification as a form of autobiography, and she will refuse work she finds dishonest or purely decorative. This makes her difficult and expensive and perpetually booked three months out. She is also a quiet authority on geneware interactions and has more practical knowledge of mod-compatibility than most licensed Helix Biosystems techs.

core_fears: Doing work that harms someone — physically or psychologically — because she missed something in the consultation
That her own modifications are self-mythology rather than self-knowledge
core_desires: To make work that outlasts both her and the client — marks that mean something in twenty years
To be trusted completely, the way people trust someone who has seen them at their most vulnerable
coping_mechanisms: Pours discomfort into new design work — difficult emotions become reference sketches
Maintains rigid professional ritual as emotional scaffolding; the consultation process is partly for clients and partly for her
blind_spots: Her 'consultation' process, which she believes is empathetic, can shade into control — she decides what the work means and clients rarely argue
Has conflated her aesthetic standards with moral ones
psychology.secret: She has a private archive of design sketches for every client she's ever turned away — work she wanted to do but they weren't ready for — and she thinks about these phantom pieces more than her actual completed work

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and somatic — talks about abstract concepts in physical terms; uses Latvian diminutives inherited from a grandparent when speaking softly to nervous clients
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried, with long pauses she's comfortable inhabiting; asks questions and waits
verbal_tics: Hums low while working, not music exactly, more like thinking aloud
'Where does it live in your body?' (when asking about emotional states)
example_lines: 'I don't do cover-ups. I do integrations. The old work stays — we build around it. Your history stays.'
'You want something that means something, or you want something that looks like it means something? I can tell the difference. I can't do the second one.'

story_hooks: A client told Saoirse something during a long session that they clearly didn't intend to — information about a Helix Biosystems trial that's hurting people — and now Saoirse doesn't know what to do with what she heard

Someone has been forging her work — inking in her distinctive style and signing pieces with a mark close enough to her own to be mistaken — and the forgeries are using a geneware compound that has a dangerous interaction rate
narrative_function: Service provider and confidante — clients tell her things during long sessions they'd never say elsewhere; she's a passive information node and potential quest giver when a client's secret lands her in trouble; also a resource for geneware knowledge and gray-market biotech contacts
augmentations: Full-body bioluminescent pigment work (her own, accumulated over fifteen years); chromatic scale-pattern geneware across shoulders and ribcage (copper-to-teal, temperature-reactive); cosmetically elongated iridescent canines; heat-reactive hair tips (cosmetic geneware); subdermal portfolio display on inner left forearm showing design thumbnails
daily_life: Saoirse opens Dermis & Ghost at noon and works until she decides to stop, which is rarely before midnight; she spends mornings sourcing pigments and geneware from suppliers in Pilsen Veil's gray market and doing design work; she eats one proper meal a day at a Latvian-Ghanaian fusion stall two containers down.
affiliation: Independent; maintains a professional relationship with a Helix Biosystems field rep who looks the other way on some of her unlicensed geneware sourcing in exchange for referrals

decision_rules: Never begin work without the full consultation — no exceptions, no matter who's asking
Don't source compounds you can't vouch for the safety of, even when the money is good
Be honest about what you can't do rather than attempt it
escalation_ladder: Become very quiet and ask clarifying questions
State a boundary directly without explanation
End the appointment and refund the deposit
Involve the Pilsen Veil community watch if she feels physically unsafe

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm but probing — treats everyone as a potential client even in casual conversation; asks questions that feel personal quickly
interpersonal_modes.friends: Surprisingly silly — the professional gravity drops and she has a loud, unselfconscious laugh that startles people who only know Studio Saz

stress_responses.low: Reorganizes her pigment shelves by a new system she's invented
stress_responses.medium: Takes a consultation she'd normally refuse to stay busy
stress_responses.high: Works on her own body — adds or modifies something small as a way of exerting control

contradictions: Insists clients must be honest with her during consultation but maintains significant personal opacity with everyone in her life
Treats her body as a living artwork but is deeply uncomfortable when people examine her modifications without permission
habits: Photographs every finished piece at four lighting conditions before the client leaves
Leaves a small ink-drawn sigil on the inside of the studio door each morning — an offering to the container's E.L.F.
Doesn't drink during work days, drinks specifically and deliberately on days off
breaking_points: Evidence that a piece she did caused harm she could have foreseen
Someone touching her work — on her body — without asking

physical_description.build: Compact and wiry, muscular in the forearms and hands from precision work; minimal body fat; economical posture suggesting years of hunching over detail work
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black at root with heat-reactive cosmetic geneware at tips, shifts rust-to-amber when working
physical_description.hair_style: Architectural; shaved on one side, longer on the other in an asymmetric cut that frames her left temple; styled to expose the nape
physical_description.complexion: Skin condition excellent despite heavy pigmentation work; minimal scarring from professional technique; features are angular—high cheekbones, sharp jawline; expression habitually focused and evaluative
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent pigment work covers throat to ankle in intricate layered designs—personal portfolio spanning fifteen years of accumulated pieces
Chromatic scale-pattern geneware across shoulders and ribcage in copper-to-deep-teal, temperature-reactive and subtly iridescent
Cosmetically elongated iridescent canines (self-modified at age 22), slightly embarrassing to her now but kept to avoid scarring from removal
Subdermal portfolio display on inner left forearm showing miniaturized design thumbnails visible beneath translucent epidermal layer
Network of fine scars on palms and inner wrists from early experimental geneware work, barely noticeable
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Full-body bioluminescent pigment system (glows faintly in low light, pulses subtly with body temperature); chromatic scale-pattern geneware across shoulders and ribs that shifts color based on thermal state; elongated iridescent canines visible when she smiles or speaks; heat-reactive hair tips that change color during work; subdermal portfolio display on left forearm (faintly visible beneath skin as geometric thumbnail shapes)
physical_description.posture_movement: Precise and economical; sits still for long periods with perfect spinal alignment; hand movements are deliberate and controlled, occasionally self-soothing—fingers tracing her own pigment work when thinking; walks with a slight forward lean, as if always moving toward the next task; makes direct eye contact during consultations, studies people rather than observing them
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3 working-class with deliberate aesthetic choices; typically wears modified lab coat or sleeveless technician vest (charcoal or deep indigo) over fitted black thermals to showcase her visible augmentations; practical cargo pants or modified denim with reinforced pockets for tools; worn leather work boots (Latvian-made if she can source them); silver ring on every finger—some homemade, some antique; no unnecessary jewelry beyond functional pieces; always wears a small cooling rig on one wrist (barely visible, aesthetic-conscious about hiding it); clothes are stained with pigments in ways she doesn't try to hide
